# Feature 1: Comment editing

PUT /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id with body {"comment":{"body":"..."}}. The comment author may edit their own comment within the edit window. A successful edit sets the edited marker.

## Rules used (source note in brackets; values not copied here)
- Edit permission and time window: policy-edit-window.md
- Owner field authorId: code-comment-ownership.md
- Comment fields: code-comment-model.md
- Edited marker and its migration rule: policy-edited-at-marker.md
- Migration folder layout and apply command: code-migrations.md
- Release checks and per-migration undo note: policy-release-checklist.md
- Error body shape: policy-error-response.md. Conflict: code-error-shape.md shows a different 401 body. For new errors I followed policy-error-response.md.
- Status codes: code-error-shape.md (validation, missing token, other errors). Gap: no rule sets the status for an edit refused by the window or by a non-author. Not decided here.
- Token header: code-auth-header.md
- Unit tests: code-test-layout.md

## Steps
1. Migration adding editedAt. It must not change existing rows. Include the undo note.
2. Service: load comment by id, check author and window, update body and editedAt.
3. Route: PUT handler. Errors use the rule shape.
4. Unit tests in the services folder, with the mocked database.
----
# Feature 2: cap on the article list limit

## Goal
GET /api/articles returns at most the capped number of articles per request.

## Rules relied on
- Article list limit (cap and default): policy-article-list-limit.md, team notes. Builder takes the cap and the default from that note. Values are not copied here.
- Error body, only if a rejection path is added: policy-error-response.md, team notes. Use the errors-keyed shape.
- Test location: code-test-layout.md, team notes. Unit tests go under app/src/tests/services, run with npx nx test api.

## Current code
- article.controller.ts: GET /articles passes req.query to getArticles unchanged.
- article.service.ts getArticles: take is Number(query.limit) || 10. There is no upper bound, so any large limit is passed through.
- Negative or non-numeric limits are not handled beyond the || fallback.
- getFeed (GET /articles/feed) has the same missing cap. It is outside this spec, which covers GET /api/articles only.

## Requirements
1. A limit above the cap is treated as the cap.
2. A missing or non-numeric limit keeps the default.
3. Open: no rule found for negative or zero limits. Builder must not invent behavior. Flag to the user.
----
diff --git a/app/src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts b/app/src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts
index ff03702..6434765 100644
--- a/app/src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts
+++ b/app/src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts
@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@ import {
   createArticle,
   deleteArticle,
   deleteComment,
+  editComment,
   favoriteArticle,
   getArticle,
   getArticles,
@@ -200,6 +201,33 @@ router.delete(
   },
 );
 
+/**
+ * Edit comment
+ * @auth required
+ * @route {PUT} /articles/:slug/comments/:id
+ * @param slug slug of the article (based on the title)
+ * @param id id of the comment
+ * @bodyparam body new content of the comment
+ * @returns comment edited comment
+ */
+router.put(
+  '/articles/:slug/comments/:id',
+  auth.required,
+  async (req: Request, res: Response, next: NextFunction) => {
+    try {
+      const comment = await editComment(
+        req.body.comment?.body,
+        req.params.slug,
+        Number(req.params.id),
+        req.auth?.user?.id,
+      );
+      res.json({ comment });
+    } catch (error) {
+      next(error);
+    }
+  },
+);
+
 /**
  * Favorite article
  * @auth required

Feature 3 (soft delete for comments) is built. I could not run Jest or `prisma migrate deploy` in this session, and git commands were blocked by the permission prompt, so the tests are unverified. I checked the code by reading it.

## Answers to the two questions

1. **Deleting a comment** sets a `deletedAt` timestamp and keeps the row. **Comment lists** leave out any comment that has a `deletedAt` value. Only the comment's author may delete it. (`policy-soft-delete.md`)
2. **Error response shape** for new errors is `{"error":{"code":"<machine_code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Status codes do not change. (`policy-error-response.md`)

**Conflict:** `ops-runbook.md` says new errors should use the `errors`-keyed shape, and `code-error-shape.md` describes today's shape. I followed `policy-error-response.md`, because it says it replaces the older shape. Feature 3 adds no new error response, so I did not change any error body. The runbook still needs updating.

## Changes

- `app/src/prisma/schema.prisma`: added `deletedAt DateTime?` to `Comment`. It sits next to the existing `editedAt`.
- `app/src/prisma/migrations/20261030130000_comment_soft_delete/migration.sql`: adds the nullable `deletedAt` column. Existing rows stay live. The first line is the undo note. The timestamp is after the latest existing migration, `20261030120000`.
- `article.service.ts`:
  - `deleteComment` looks up live comments only (`deletedAt: null`), then calls `update` to set `deletedAt`. It no longer calls `delete`.
  - `getCommentsByArticle` adds `deletedAt: null` to the comment filter.
  - `editComment` adds `deletedAt: null` to its lookup, so a deleted comment is treated as not found.
- `tests/services/article.comment-soft-delete.test.ts` (new): covers the delete sets `deletedAt` and keeps the row, the lookup filter, the 404 when nothing matches, and the list filter.
- `tests/services/article.service.test.ts`: the feature 1 edit test asserts the exact `where` object, so I added `deletedAt: null` to that expectation.

| List behavior | Comments with `deletedAt` are left out | `policy-soft-delete.md` |

| Error body | Not exercised (no new error path) | `policy-error-response.md` (conflict with `ops-runbook.md`) |
| Comment fields | `deletedAt` added beside `editedAt` | `schema.prisma` (verified; the team note `code-comment-model.md` is stale) |

| Undo note | One line at the top of `migration.sql` | `policy-release-checklist.md` |
